label: Brent Crude
value: $98.44/bbl Sep 23 (-0.82%), first sustained drop below $100 in weeks after Saudi Arabia restarted its East-West pipeline Sep 22, down from $101.61 at the Sep 21 close
delta: Fell below $100 for the first time in weeks after Saudi Arabia restarted the East-West pipeline Sep 22 and seven supertankers loaded 14M barrels via Hormuz over the weekend; extended the slide to $98.44 Sep 23 (WTI -1.34% to $89.31) as markets weighed Iran's roadmap for a phased Hormuz reopening

label: Saudi East-West Pipeline
value: Restarted Sep 22 at a reduced rate after roughly two weeks shut; Aramco targeting a return toward ~4M bpd (4% of global supply), full commercial resumption still estimated to take weeks
contestNote: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright had said the outage would be 'measured in days'; UK officials and some industry sources cited five-to-six-week repair estimates -- the Sep 22 restart, roughly 11-12 days after the Sep 10-11 shutdown, landed closer to Wright's framing, though a security source cautions full resumption could still take additional weeks
delta: Restarted pumping Tuesday Sep 22 after seven supertankers (14M bbl combined) loaded via Hormuz over the preceding weekend as a stopgap; one cargo was scheduled to load at Yanbu for China as flows resumed

label: Saudi Crude Loadings vs. Pre-Crisis
delta: Replacement flow moving via Sohar ship-to-ship transfers and the Strait of Hormuz itself (2M+ bpd), a smaller volume via Suez/Sumed, and limited use of the much longer Cape of Good Hope route

label: Bab el-Mandeb Daily Transits
delta: New second chokepoint risk: Houthi capture of Yemen's Mokha port and advance toward the strait cut Red Sea vessel crossings from 30 (Wed) to 12 (Thu), narrowing the Suez/Red Sea bypass route shippers have used to avoid the closed Strait of Hormuz

label: US Diesel Price
delta: Crossed $6/gallon for the first time as the Sep 9-10 shipping-attack wave and the new Red Sea front pushed Brent toward its $108 crisis peak

label: FAO Food Price Index
source: FAO (Aug 2026, released Sep 4 -- highest since late 2022)
delta: Up 1.9% from July's revised level and 2.5% y/y; broad-based across all five commodity groups -- sugar +11.9% m/m, cereals +2.2% m/m (highest since May 2024), dairy +2.3% m/m

label: Hormuz Daily Tanker Transits
value: 2 vessels Mon Sep 21 (down from 10 Sun); Iran floats a phased reopening within a week if the US eases its naval blockade
contestNote: CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper said oil and LNG shipments through the strait hit a six-month high over the preceding two weeks, topping 1 billion barrels; independent tracking counted just two trackable commodity vessels crossing Sep 21, against a pre-war daily average of roughly 125 large commercial vessels
delta: A tanker (LR Stephanie) and a separate LPG carrier (Al Maryah) were both struck by unidentified projectiles Sep 21, the same day transits collapsed to 2 vessels from 10 the day before
deltaNote: Iran's Foreign Ministry says the strait could reopen within a week if Washington lifts its naval blockade and eases military pressure, per the roadmap Tehran presented the US Sep 23

label: War-Risk Insurance (Hull Value)
value: 7.5-10% (a $100M tanker now faces $3-10M in war-risk premiums)
source: Lloyd's List / Discovery Alert / Aju Press (Sep 15, 2026)
delta: vs 0.125-0.25% pre-crisis; container surcharges now running $1,800-3,800 per box plus an extra $1,000/container for Hormuz transits

label: 2026 Global Growth Forecast
contestNote: World Bank warns growth could fall to 1.3% in an adverse energy-shock scenario; IMF's own baseline is more optimistic at 3.1%
